articles.title: Rust Is Eating JavaScript (Still, in 2026)
articles.description: Our most-read link of 2021 gets an update for 2026. Lee Robinson (then Vercel, now Cursor) predicted Rust would be used to reimplement more and more JavaScript ecosystem tooling, and Rspack, Biome, Turbopack, and Bun's recent rewrite keep proving him right.
articles.author: Lee Robinson

articles.title: Octane: React's Programming Model, But Compiled
articles.description: From the creator of Inferno comes a successor: a compiled React-like framework (differences explained here) that generates reactivity ahead of time with no VDOM. Supports TSX/JSX and TSRX, with integrations for TanStack Query and Router, plus other common React libraries.
articles.author: Dominic Gannaway

articles.title: ▶  The Creator of TypeScript Shows Off TypeScript 7
articles.description: Anders Hejlsberg demos the 10x speedup gained by the new Go-based TypeScript compiler on VS Code's 1.3M line codebase. He also covers the new LSP language server and why compiler API users (Vue, Astro, Svelte) must stay on TypeScript 6.
articles.author: Anders Hejlsberg (Microsoft)

articles.title: Domenic Denicola's Agentic Coding Setup
articles.description: It's fascinating when a prolific developer (Domenic was a key figure in the adoption of promises in JavaScript, creating jsdom, and much more) shares their workflow. This is no exception, covering areas like disposable VMs, Tailscale, and worktrees.
articles.author: Domenic Denicola

articles.title: How Medium Built Its New 'Table of Contents' Feature
articles.description: How the content site built a dynamic table of contents widget for all its articles, inspired by a third-party Chrome extension that did the same thing.
articles.author: Scott Batson (Medium)

articles.title: 🌐 MapLibre GL JS 6.0: Interactive Vector Maps for the Web
articles.description: A WebGL-powered library for rendering interactive vector tile maps, forked from Mapbox GL JS after its 2020 relicensing. Version 6 goes ESM-only, requires WebGL 2, and lands broad performance gains. Release notes and a v5 to v6 migration guide.
articles.author: MapLibre

articles.title: Bruno 4.0: An Open-Source HTTP API Client App
articles.description: An open source, JavaScript-powered lightweight alternative to something like Postman for testing and making requests against HTTP APIs.
articles.author: Anoop M D, Anusree P S and Contributors

articles.title: tslog 5: Zero-Dependency Logger for Node, Deno, Bun and Browsers
articles.description: A ground-up rewrite, now ESM-only, and also covers workers and React Native. Pretty output by default, JSON optionally, plus middleware, file/HTTP/worker transports, secret masking, and error stacks that resolve through source maps to your original .ts lines. GitHub repo.
articles.author: Eugene Terehov

articles.title: eslint-package-json: Powerful ESLint Rules for package.json
articles.description: An ESLint plugin that catches package.json mistakes like invalid names, bad version ranges, broken exports, redundant files entries, and more, and fixes many of them automatically.
articles.author: Sindre Sorhus

articles.title: Shadscan: Deterministic UI Audits for shadcn Apps
articles.description: A tool that statically analyzes your shadcn components using almost 60 deterministic checks (no AI or API keys needed) around fundamental accessibility, state, and composition best practices.
articles.author: OrcDev

articles.description: 😄 htmx 4.0 is, curiously, pitching itself as "the first JavaScript library to release exclusively on the Game Boy" with a commemorative cartridge.
At last week's TC39 meeting, Await Dictionary (Promise.allKeyed) progressed to Stage 3.
Ryan Dahl says that deno compile will soon support using QuickJS instead of V8 for making radically smaller binaries from JS/TS projects.
Node.js has a new API docs site in preview (now includes search!)
Oxlint's type-aware linting is now stable.
pnpm has had a flurry of releases introducing native workspace release management, a doctor command to diagnose installation issues, and more.
React 19.2.8, 19.1.9 and 19.0.8 to fix a potential DoS vulnerability in server function endpoints.
Ember 7.1 – Adds a wide variety of new helpers and operators, and docs modernization.
Nuxt 4.5.1 and 3.21.10 – Security patch releases after last week's big Nuxt 4.5 release.
ESLint 10.8, Deno 2.9.4, Prisma 7.9, React Router 8.3, Vue 3.6 RC2

articles.title: WOFF 1.0 at 16: The Format That Made Web Fonts Work
articles.description: Did you know @font-face was adopted into CSS2 in 1998? But it sat largely unused amid fights over licensing, obfuscation and DRM. Chris Lilley, PNG co-author and author of W3C's 1996 case for fonts on the web, explains how the deadlock broke with the “entirely DRM-free” format we know and love.
articles.author: Chris Lilley (W3C)

articles.title: ∞ To infinity and Beyond, in CSS
articles.description: e, pi, infinity, and NaN are all widely supported constants accepted in CSS math functions, and Adam runs through several ways going to infinity can improve your designs.
articles.author: Adam Argyle

articles.title: The Launch of CodePen 2.0
articles.description: CodePen has been a reliable piece of web development infrastructure for 14 years and now the experience has gone 2.0 with an all-new editor, and lots of goodies for paid users like the ability to quickly deploy pens to a CodePen subdomain.
articles.author: Chris Coyier

articles.title: When You Need To Make a Triangle, Think Conic Gradients
articles.description: conic-gradient() is more flexible than you might imagine! You can make pie segments, ray bursts, or triangles, and use transitions on them too.
articles.author: Chris Coyier

articles.title: Measuring Component Performance with the Container Timing API
articles.description: Chrome's origin trial for the Container Timing API lets you tag a DOM region with a containertiming attribute and track each contentful part as it paints. It won't tell you when a component is finished, though.
articles.author: Harry Roberts

articles.title: Paint the Static Image First, Fetch the Animation After
articles.description: Andy's elaborate animated banner weighs half a megabyte, so now a static AVIF paints first with the animated SVG only fetched on screens big enough to do it justice.
articles.author: Andy Clarke

articles.title: Handling Concurrency on the Web with Web Locks API
articles.description: A practical walkthrough of stopping multiple tabs from racing each other, thanks to the widely available Web Locks API.
articles.author: Cesar Contreras

articles.title: The Core Web Vitals Thresholds You Trust Might Be Wrong
articles.description: RUM data from ten retailers suggests Google's 2.5s 'good' LCP threshold is too lenient, with optimal engagement arriving between 100ms and 1 second.
articles.author: Tammy Everts

articles.title: Stolen Buttons
articles.description: One designer's hobby is 'stealing' buttons from the sites they visit. It's quite the collection and certainly reflects the current design zeitgeist. There's a browser extension if you want to make your own similar hoard.
articles.author: Anatoly Zenkov

articles.title: Canvas UI: A Creative Canvas and WebGL Component Library
articles.description: An open source, framework agnostic library of cutting edge HTML-in-Canvas and WebGL components you can copy and paste. This has received a lot of kudos on social media this week.
articles.author: David Haz

articles.title: 🌐 MapLibre GL JS 6.0: Interactive Vector Maps for the Web
articles.description: A WebGL-powered library for rendering interactive vector tile maps. Version 6 goes ESM-only, requires WebGL 2, and lands broad performance gains. Release notes and a v5 to v6 migration guide.
articles.author: MapLibre

articles.title: Markdy: Like Mermaid but for Animations and Motion
articles.description: Instead of writing animations in CSS or JavaScript, you use a simpler language focused on core animation concepts (akin to Mermaid with diagrams). The examples are neat.
articles.author: Hoang Yell

articles.title: KaTeX: Fast Math to HTML Typesetting for the Web
articles.description: Based on Donald Knuth’s TeX, KaTeX provides a no-dependency way to rapidly render TeX math expressions in a predictable manner, regardless of environment. The sandbox demo page shows off how smooth it is.
articles.author: Emily Eisenberg and Sophie Alpert

articles.title: Dither It: An Online Image Dithering Tool
articles.description: Drag in an image and play around with settings, palettes, and more to get the vibe you want. Josh W. Comeau recommended this tool on Bluesky recently, and his thread has much better examples than my attempt above… 😅
articles.author: Alex Harris
